items.title: The same starts can make another world
items.description: ATTRACT and AVOID restart four walkers from the same seed and positions. Advance an equal number of fixed steps, then compare the marks. Pink shows current scent; white height retains accumulated visits; cyan marks current positions.

items.title: Random Remove
items.description: Keep the eligibility argument; hand off to the actual next hall, 10 PRINT.
items.before: Ask now whether a random choice can be fair to a cube that was grey. Within the amber set the draw is even; the grey were decided before it ran, by a rule you can read and change, and the seed that makes a run repeatable has no say in it. Carry the changing set into the next room, where a walker takes its steps from draws like these and the set of places it can reach is decided one step at a time.
items.after: Ask now whether a random choice can be fair to a cube that was grey. Within the amber set the draw is even; the grey were decided before it ran, by a rule you can read and change, and the seed that makes a run repeatable has no say in it. In the next room, the available choice narrows to two diagonal marks. Follow what their neighbours make of them: when does a choice become a contour, and when can that contour become a passage?

items.title: Random Pheromone
items.description: Keep the chapter’s question about possible worlds while making its proposed avoidance comparison available to the visitor.
items.before: A walker that avoided the strongest trace would make a different world from the same act of leaving marks. That comparison is an available direction for development rather than a control offered here. Next, the noise mixer returns to field construction: several contributions at different scales will combine without depending on a history of visits.
items.after: Could the same act of leaving marks help make a different world? Note the step count, press AVOID and advance to the same count. The terrain and scent clear, and the four walkers begin again from the same seeded positions; this time the signal-guided choice favours the weakest scent. Compare the resulting visits before deciding what the changed rule did. REPLAY restarts the selected rule. Both experiments use the same fixed decay interval per step, although their paths can cause later random draws to be used differently at the boundary. Next, the noise mixer returns to field construction: several contributions at different scales will combine without depending on a history of visits.
